drills.title: Which TECC Phase?
drills.description: Each action belongs to a phase. Do the right thing in the wrong zone and you become a casualty.

items.prompt: Applying a tourniquet 'high and tight' while rounds are still being fired.
items.why: Tourniquet is the only medical intervention in direct threat.

items.prompt: Packing a groin (junctional) wound with hemostatic gauze in a cleared hallway.
items.why: Junctional packing is warm-zone (indirect threat) care.

items.prompt: Placing a vented chest seal under police escort.
items.why: Respiration step of MARCH — indirect threat.

items.prompt: Dragging a casualty behind a concrete pillar.
items.why: Moving to cover is direct-threat care.

items.prompt: Reassessing tourniquet effectiveness and documenting time in the ambulance.
items.why: Reassessment and documentation continue during evacuation care.

items.prompt: Needle decompression for suspected tension pneumothorax at the CCP.
Telling a wounded officer to apply his own tourniquet while staying in the fight.
items.why: Self-aid is emphasized under direct threat.

items.prompt: Wrapping a casualty in a hypothermia blanket before moving to the CCP.
items.why: Hypothermia prevention starts in indirect threat.

items.prompt: Starting a second IV and advanced monitoring en route to the trauma center.
Placing an NPA and recovery position in an unconscious casualty in a cleared room.
items.why: Airway management is deferred until indirect threat.

items.prompt: Converting a hasty tourniquet to a pressure dressing when safe and time allows.
items.why: TQ reassessment/conversion happens in indirect threat or later.
